ROLES.md:104-107 records the operator's 2026-08-19 ruling: 'There is no fleet or per-provider cap on parallel workers... the only numeric bound is the recursion depth cap.' subdelegation.md:15 already reflects this correctly ('no fleet cap... operator's ruling 2026-08-19: no DeepSeek rate-limit cap'). archaeology.kind: contradicted schema rule — a stated requirement that the schema, the machine-readable copy, and the majority of committed instances all disagree with
archaeology.citation: docs/infra/agents/manager-brief-template.md:105; contrast findings/README.md (§Schema, 'claims' required-but-not-non-empty), docs/infra/agents/findings-schema.json:26 ('Empty array when none are touched'), docs/infra/delegation/DELEGATEE.md:251 ('claims and new_rows stay empty in a dump')
archaeology.detail: manager-brief-template.md's findings-collection checklist (item 3) states: 'Required fields present — task_id, date, model and the claims array must be non-empty per findings/README.md.' findings/README.md contains no such non-empty requirement (claims is simply a required array, explicitly allowed to be []). The machine-readable schema copy explicitly documents claims as 'Empty array when none are touched.' DELEGATEE.md's own reporting section instructs context dumps to keep claims empty by design. Sampled committed findings files confirm empty-claims is the norm for analysis/census/audit tasks, not an exception (findings/T410-instruction-audit.json, T507-scaling-census.json, T575-s03-queue-layer-audit.json, T579-decision-log-study.json all ship claims:[]). A manager literally following this checklist item would reject a large fraction of conforming findings files as defective.

archaeology.kind: the composed-preamble's own provenance claim is false for one section; the seed's role-variant goal is unbuilt
archaeology.detail: cmdOrient prints '## principles (extracted from AGENTS.md / DELEGATEE.md / sprint.md / DIRECTION.md)' immediately above 8 lines that are Zig string literals baked into main.zig at build time, not read from any of the four named files at compose time (confirmed by reading the function body: no file I/O touches AGENTS.md/DELEGATEE.md/sprint.md/DIRECTION.md anywhere in cmdOrient). This is the inverse of the S05 seed's stated goal for orient ('a current, contradiction-free, role-sized orientation composed at read time from the store and a small set of audited sources') — today's principles section is neither derived from the sources nor guaranteed to track them if they change. Separately, cmdOrient discards its args parameter entirely (`_ = args;`), confirming the seed's §3.3 'orient --role <r>' variants do not exist yet; this is a gap for the S05 audit/spec phases to fill, not a contradiction in current text, so it is graded 'should' rather than 'must'.
